question: Discuss different types of test doubles (mock, stub, spy, fake). When should you avoid mocking, and what are the signs of over-mocking?

keyPoints: Stub: provides canned responses to calls, no behavior verification
Mock: verifies interactions (method calls, parameters), behavior-based testing
Spy: partial mock wrapping real object, can verify and use real methods
Fake: working implementation but simplified (in-memory database)
Over-mocking signs: tests become brittle, test implementation not behavior, changes break many tests
Avoid mocking value objects, entities, and internal implementation details
expectedAnswer.explanation: Choose test doubles based on testing goals. Use stubs for dependencies that provide data (repositories returning test data). Use mocks when verifying interactions is important (checking email was sent). Spies useful for testing legacy code. Fakes for complex dependencies (in-memory H2 instead of PostgreSQL). Over-mocking occurs when tests know too much about implementation: testing private methods, mocking everything including value objects, verifying every method call. Signs: tests break with refactoring that doesn't change behavior. Better: test public API, mock only at boundaries (external services), prefer real objects when practical.
